result.title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
result.summary: Relational deep learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning end-to-end predictive models over relational databases by representing them as temporal heterogeneous graphs. Recent advances based on graph neural networks and Transformers have achieved strong performance across diverse domains. However, the effectiveness of simpler relational baselines remains underexplored, making it difficult to assess how much architectural complexity is needed to achieve strong predictive performance. Motivated by the observation that predictive signals arise from target attributes, relational attributes, and historical labels, we revisit how effectively these signals can be exploited using simple propagation methods. We adapt fixed low-pass feature propagation to relational entity graphs and train an MLP for prediction. The resulting predictions are further refined using Correct-and-Smooth, a graph-based label propagation algorithm that incorporates historical labels over task-specific meta-graphs connecting target entities. Across classification and regression tasks on RelBench, an MLP trained on neighborhood-filtered features outperforms one using only target-entity features on most tasks and recovers a substantial portion of the performance of heterogeneous GNNs. Correct-and-Smooth provides further gains from historical labels, although applying it requires a separately constructed meta-graph because connections among target entities are not directly specified by the relational entity graph. Together, our studies revisit the effectiveness of established propagation methods as simple RDL baselines while identifying canonical meta-graph construction as a key challenge for effective label propagation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 RelBench 上重新审视关系深度学习的简单基线：把固定低通特征传播用于关系实体图并训练 MLP 做预测，再用 Correct-and-Smooth 图标签传播结合历史标签精化结果，并指出目标实体间需单独构建元图。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定传播 + 简单预测头」基线及基于元图的标签传播迭代精化，可能为 LVR 中潜在状态的传播式更新、简单基线与复杂架构的收益对照提供可供核查的方法线索，但与多模态推理的可迁移性尚不清楚。
